1.q: Which state government in 2025 declared the two Harappan sites Tighrana and Mitathal as archaeological sites?
1.explanation: Tighrana and Mitathal are Harappan archaeological sites in Haryana; Haryana declared them archaeological sites.

2.q: Arrange the following phases of the French Revolution in the correct chronological order: I. Dictatorship of Bonaparte; II. Convention; III. National Assembly; IV. Rule of the Directory.
2.explanation: The National Assembly came first, followed by the Convention, the Directory and then Bonaparte’s dictatorship: III, II, IV, I (option C).

3.q: The Suez Crisis of 1956 involved which country nationalising the Suez Canal?
3.explanation: Egyptian President Gamal Abdel Nasser nationalised the Suez Canal in 1956, triggering the Suez Crisis.

4.q: Who made the remark, “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it”?
4.explanation: The “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it” slogan is attributed to Bal Gangadhar Tilak (option B).

5.q: With reference to the proposals of the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946), consider these statements: I. The Constituent Assembly was to be formed through indirect elections by the Provincial Legislative Assemblies. II. The Princely States could send representatives to the Constituent Assembly. Which statement or statements are correct?
5.explanation: Provincial representatives were indirectly elected by their legislatures; princely-state representatives were nominated by their rulers. Both statements are correct (C).

6.q: Which amendment is related to the Goods and Services Tax?
6.explanation: The Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016 introduced the GST framework.

7.q: Under the Constitution of India, the Supreme Court is empowered to settle disputes between the Centre and the States through which jurisdiction?
7.explanation: Article 131 gives the Supreme Court original jurisdiction over specified disputes between the Union and States.

8.q: With reference to the Viksit Bharat–Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025, which statement is true?

opts.a: It reduces the statutory employment guarantee from 125 to 100 days.
opts.b: It applies only to urban local bodies.
opts.c: It eliminates the rural employment guarantee entirely.
opts.d: It replaces MGNREGA and increases the guaranteed workdays for rural households.

8.explanation: The 2025 Act replaces the MGNREGA framework and raises the annual employment guarantee from 100 to 125 days for eligible rural households (D).

9.q: The promotion of international peace and security is provided for in the Constitution of India under which part?
9.explanation: Article 51, among the Directive Principles of State Policy, directs the State to promote international peace and security.

10.q: Which article deals with the administration of tribal areas and Autonomous District Councils in North-East India under the Sixth Schedule?
10.explanation: Article 244(2) applies the Sixth Schedule provisions to the specified tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram. The stem’s phrase “through Governors’ rule” is imprecise; this is the closest constitutional provision listed.

11.q: Changes in the length of day-time and night-time across different seasons are caused by:

opts.a: Earth’s revolution round the sun in an elliptical manner
opts.d: Revolution of the Earth on a tilted axis

11.explanation: Earth’s axial tilt combined with its revolution around the Sun changes the angle and duration of sunlight received through the year (D).

12.q: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched? I. Apogee – the Moon’s orbit is farthest from the Earth. II. Aphelion – the Earth is closest to the Sun. Select the correct code.
12.explanation: Apogee is the farthest point in the Moon’s orbit from Earth, so statement I is correct. Aphelion is Earth’s farthest point from the Sun, not its closest, so only I is correct (A).

13.q: Recent scientific research indicates that the Indian tectonic plate is splitting into two layers deep beneath the Tibetan Plateau. What is this process called?
13.explanation: Lithospheric delamination is the peeling or detachment of dense lower lithosphere from the overlying plate (D).

14.q: Consider these statements: I. The length of the monsoon season becomes shorter moving from southern India towards northern India. II. In the northern plains, annual rainfall declines from east to west. Which statement or statements are correct?
14.explanation: The rainy season generally lasts longer in southern India and becomes shorter farther north; rainfall across the northern plains also generally decreases from east to west. Both statements are correct (C).

22.q: With reference to IUCN and CITES, consider these statements: I. IUCN is an organ of the United Nations and CITES is an international agreement between governments. II. IUCN runs thousands of field projects around the world to better manage natural environments. III. CITES is legally binding on its member States, but does not replace national laws. 23.q: Consider these statements about Article 4 of the Paris Agreement: I. It is central to global climate action and is often cited in climate negotiations. II. It requires all Parties to prepare, communicate and maintain successive Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs). III. It mandates legally binding emission-reduction targets for both developed and developing countries. Which option is correct?

opts.a: Both II and III are correct, and both explain I
opts.b: Both II and III are correct, but only one explains I
opts.c: Only statement II is correct, and it explains I
opts.d: Neither statement II nor III is correct

23.explanation: Article 4 requires each Party to prepare and communicate successive NDCs. It does not impose identical legally binding emission-reduction targets; the content of the targets is nationally determined. Thus only II is correct (C).

24.q: Consider these statements: I. In India, Biodiversity Management Committees play a crucial role in achieving the objectives of the Nagoya Protocol. II. These committees have responsibilities in access and benefit-sharing, including imposing collection charges for use of biological resources within their jurisdiction. Which statement or statements are correct?
24.explanation: Biodiversity Management Committees support local biodiversity governance and access-and-benefit-sharing, including collection fees for biological resources. Both statements are correct (C).

25.q: With reference to Eco-Sensitive Zones, consider these statements: I. They are areas notified under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. II. They ban all forms of human activity within their boundaries except agriculture. Which statement or statements are correct?
25.explanation: Eco-Sensitive Zones are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, not the Wildlife (Protection) Act. Activities are prohibited, regulated or permitted; they are not all banned. Both statements are false (D).

29.q: With reference to microsatellite DNA, consider these statements: I. It consists of short tandemly repeated nucleotide sequences. II. It is highly polymorphic and varies among individuals. III. It is widely used in DNA fingerprinting and population genetics. IV. It directly codes for proteins involved in cellular metabolism. Which statements are correct?
29.explanation: Microsatellites are short tandem repeats, are highly variable and are useful in DNA fingerprinting and population genetics. They are not protein-coding sequences; I, II and III are correct (C).

30.q: With reference to rare-earth minerals, consider these statements: I. They consist of metallic elements including the lanthanides. II. They are used in high-technology products such as smartphones and wind turbines. III. They are abundantly found in pure form in nature. IV. They are important in renewable-energy and defence technologies. Which statements are correct?
30.explanation: Rare-earth elements include the lanthanides and are used in electronics, wind turbines and defence technologies. They are not generally found in abundant pure form; I, II and IV are correct (B).

31.q: Which indicators are used in the Statistical Handbook of Mizoram to assess the State’s fiscal health? I. Gross Fiscal Deficit as a percentage of GSDP. II. Outstanding Debt-to-GSDP ratio. III. Revenue Surplus/Deficit. IV. Current Account Deficit. Select the correct answer.
31.explanation: Gross fiscal deficit, outstanding debt relative to GSDP, and revenue balance are State fiscal indicators. Current-account deficit is an external-sector measure, not a state-budget indicator. I, II and III are correct (C).

33.q: Which districts of Mizoram have Autonomous District Councils?
33.explanation: Mizoram’s three Autonomous District Councils are in the Lai, Mara and Chakma areas, located in Lawngtlai and Siaha districts (B).

34.q: Which banking indicator is used to assess credit flow in Mizoram?
34.explanation: The Credit–Deposit Ratio compares credit extended by banks with deposits mobilised and is commonly used to assess local credit flow (A).

35.q: Which sector contributes the largest share to Mizoram’s Gross State Domestic Product?
35.explanation: The services sector contributes the largest share to Mizoram’s GSDP (C).

36.q: With reference to Mizoram’s geography, consider these statements: I. Mizoram lies entirely in the Purvanchal Hill range. II. The State extends farther north–south than east–west. III. Most rivers of Mizoram drain into the Bay of Bengal. Which statements are correct?
36.explanation: Mizoram is part of the Purvanchal hills, has a longer north–south than east–west extent, and most rivers drain southward through the Kolodyne/Karnaphuli systems toward the Bay of Bengal. All three statements are correct (D).

37.q: With reference to health indicators in Mizoram, consider these statements: I. Infant Mortality Rate in Mizoram is lower than the national average. II. Health statistical data are drawn from the Civil Registration System. III. The Universal Immunisation Programme is implemented through the Integrated Child Development Service (ICDS). Which statements are correct?
37.reviewNote: Held out: official IMR estimates use the Sample Registration System, while the statement broadly attributes health statistics to the Civil Registration System. UIP is delivered through the health system with ICDS coordination, making the wording and available combinations insufficiently precise for a unique answer.
37.explanation: Mizoram has reported a lower IMR than the national average, but official IMR estimates are based on the Sample Registration System. ICDS functionaries support immunisation outreach, while UIP is a health programme. The broad wording does not make the offered combinations unambiguously correct, so the item is held out.

38.q: A train 130 metres long is travelling at 45 km/h. If it takes 30 seconds to completely cross a bridge, what is the bridge’s length?
38.explanation: At 45 km/h the train travels 12.5 m/s, so in 30 seconds it covers 375 m. This is train length plus bridge length; the bridge is 375−130=245 m (B).

39.q: A shopkeeper sells goods at a price that gives a profit of 22.5% on cost price. If total sales during a week amount to ₹392, what is the profit for that week?
39.explanation: The selling price is 122.5% of cost. Cost=₹392/1.225=₹320, so profit=₹392−₹320=₹72 (C).

opts.a: Ministry of Women and Child Development

41.explanation: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj launched the Model Women-Friendly Gram Panchayats initiative in March 2025, so D is correct.

42.q: What is the name of the Election Commission of India’s digital platform for real-time voter-turnout reporting?
42.explanation: The Election Commission’s ECINET platform consolidates its digital services, including access to polling trends and voter-turnout information.

43.q: What postal service did the Department of Posts launch in 2025 specifically to deliver educational materials?
43.explanation: Gyan Post is the Department of Posts’ 2025 service for sending educational materials, including books and study material.

44.q: What is the name of the world’s first Digital Tribal University launched in New Delhi?
44.explanation: The official description identifies Adi Sanskriti as a digital learning platform, while a full-fledged Digital Tribal University was described as an idea under exploration; the premise is not supported as written.
44.reviewNote: Held out because the official announcement describes Adi Sanskriti as a digital learning platform and says a full-fledged Digital Tribal University was only being explored; it does not support the question’s claim that a university had already been launched.

45.q: Which state ranked first in the ICJS 2.0 national rankings released in January 2026?
45.explanation: Uttarakhand ranked first in the January 2026 ICJS 2.0 dashboard standings, ahead of Haryana and Assam.

46.q: The National Sports Governance Act, partially brought into effect from 1 January 2026, primarily aims to:

opts.b: Revise eligibility criteria for Olympic selection
opts.c: Establish governance structures for national and regional sports bodies
opts.d: Create a single unified national sports team

46.explanation: The Act establishes a statutory framework for recognition, governance and oversight of national sports bodies, including their governance structures.

47.q: Which country is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit in 2026?
47.explanation: India holds the BRICS chairship in 2026 and is hosting the 18th summit.

48.q: Which country became the first to formally recognise the self-declared Republic of Somaliland as an independent and sovereign state?
48.explanation: Israel announced formal recognition of Somaliland in December 2025, becoming the first country to do so.

49.q: During German Federal Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s January 2026 visit to India, which areas were prominent in bilateral discussions?
49.explanation: The visit covered trade, defence, green development and other areas; the scan’s wording asks for a single primary focus without distinguishing among these prominent topics.
49.reviewNote: Held out because official visit materials list trade and investment, defence and security, and green and sustainable development as cooperation areas. The prompt's ‘primary focus’ wording does not distinguish among those topics, so more than one offered choice is supportable.

50.q: What initially triggered the widespread protests in Iran in 2025–26?

opts.c: An economic crisis involving soaring inflation and a collapsing currency

50.explanation: The protests began amid sharp price rises and the rial’s collapse, which intensified public anger over Iran’s economic crisis.

40.q: A bank offers 5% annual compound interest, compounded half-yearly. A customer deposits ₹1,600 on 1 January and another ₹1,600 on 1 July. What is the total interest earned at the end of the year?
40.explanation: The half-yearly rate is 2.5%. The January deposit earns ₹1,600[(1.025)²−1]=₹81; the July deposit earns ₹1,600×0.025=₹40. Total interest is ₹121 (A).

54.q: The recurring decimal 0.757575... (0.(75)) is equal to the fraction:
54.explanation: 0.757575… repeats the block 75, so it equals 75/99 = 25/33 (option A).

67.q: A can do a piece of work in 25 days and B can do it in 20 days. They work together for 5 days and then A goes away. What fraction of the work remains for B to complete?
67.explanation: Together they complete 5(1/25 + 1/20) = 45/100 of the work. The remainder is 55/100 = 11/20 (option D).

71.explanation: The numerators are consecutive squares 1², 2², 3², 4²; the next is 5² = 25. The denominators rise from 22 to 25, so the next is 26: 25/26 (option C).

91.explanation: Six of the eleven listed pack weights exceed 5 kg, so the probability is 6/11 (option B).

61.explanation: 576 = 2⁶×3². Multiplying by 3 makes each prime exponent a multiple of 3, so the smallest multiplier is 3 (B).

62.q: A two-digit number is four times the sum of its digits. If 9 is added to the number, its digits are reversed. What is the number?
62.explanation: Let the digits be a and b. The first condition gives 10a+b=4(a+b), hence b=2a. Reversal after adding 9 gives b−a=1, so a=1,b=2 and the number is 12 (D).

64.q: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a person weighing 56 kg is replaced by a new man. What is the new man’s weight?
64.explanation: The total weight increases by 8×2.5=20 kg. Replacing 56 kg with 76 kg gives that increase, so B is correct.

65.explanation: The total is 11×60=660. The first five sum to 290 and the last five to 280; the sixth observation is 660−290−280=90 (A).

73.explanation: The sequence has first term 9 and common difference −3. Its 21st term is 9+20(−3)=−51 (B).

75.explanation: The other candidate gets 28%, so the majority is 72%−28%=44% of the votes. Since 44% equals 264, the total is 600 (D).

77.explanation: At 25% higher price, the same budget buys 1/1.25=0.8 of the former quantity, a 20% reduction (B).

78.explanation: If B=100, then A=80. B exceeds A by 20/80=25% of A’s salary (A).

81.explanation: After two years, the value is P×0.8²=₹4,800. Thus P=₹4,800/0.64=₹7,500 (D).

82.explanation: The third-year growth factor is 2,662/2,420=1.10, so the annual rate is 10% (C).

83.explanation: If 12 books cost the same as 16 books sell for, then the selling price per book is 12/16=3/4 of cost. The loss is 25% (B).

92.explanation: Set πr²=2πr. For a positive radius, r=2 units (B).

The item Q37 was independently re-keyed after checking its printed wording; the final key’s answer conflicts with the standard collocation/phrase or worked calculation. The item Q77 was independently re-keyed after checking its printed wording; the final key’s answer conflicts with the standard collocation/phrase or worked calculation.

1.q: I __________ this task by lunch as it is not hard.
1.explanation: By a stated future deadline (“by lunch”), the future perfect “will have finished” is the natural choice.

2.q: Where ______, had we not met her?
2.explanation: The final key marks D, but “had we not met her” is a past unreal condition and standard grammar would use “would she have stayed”; that exact form is not offered. The printed item/key conflict, so this question is held out from scoring pending clarification.

3.q: The cheese looks as if the rats __________ it.
3.explanation: The present perfect “have nibbled” describes the apparent completed action and its present result.

4.q: __________ you all along?
4.explanation: “All along” describes an action continuing over a period up to now, so the present perfect continuous fits.

5.q: The truck hit her while she __________ the road.
5.explanation: The past continuous marks the action in progress when the truck hit her.

6.q: I wish he __________ me that he was quitting.
6.explanation: “I wish” expresses regret about an earlier omission, so the past perfect “had told” is used.

7.q: Thank you so much for the bag. I __________ one for a long time.
7.explanation: The past perfect continuous describes the wish continuing before the bag was received.

8.q: Rakesh __________ for the competition these days.
8.explanation: “These days” points to a current temporary activity, so the present continuous fits.

9.q: That man __________ at the bus stop for the last hour.
9.explanation: “For the last hour” describes an action continuing until now, so the present perfect continuous fits.

10.q: Shall I tell that person that the last bus __________?
10.explanation: The present perfect “has gone” describes the bus leaving with a present result: it is no longer available.

11.explanation: To cast a slur on someone is to insult or damage their reputation; “bringing into disrepute” matches.

12.explanation: “Feet of clay” refers to a person’s hidden weakness or flaw, so C is the closest meaning.

13.explanation: A broken reed is an unreliable source of support.

opts.c: an achievement to be proud of

14.explanation: A “bee in one’s bonnet” is a persistent preoccupation or obsession.

opts.c: to do a thing in vain

15.explanation: The idiom means to keep pursuing or discussing something with no chance of success.

16.explanation: A “wet blanket” is someone or something that dampens others’ enjoyment.

17.explanation: “All agog” means very eager or excited.

18.explanation: To “turn tail” is to flee, especially out of fear.

19.explanation: “Red tapism” means excessive official procedures and resulting bureaucratic delay.

20.explanation: “Ever and anon” means occasionally or from time to time.

21.q: He wants someone to take photographs.

opts.a: Someone is wanted to take photographs
opts.b: He wants to be taking photographs
opts.c: He wants photographs to be taken

21.explanation: The passive infinitive “photographs to be taken” preserves the meaning that he wants others to take them.

22.q: He decided that the house should be sold.

opts.a: He decided the house to be sold
opts.b: He decided to sell the house
opts.c: He has decided to sell the house
opts.d: The house was decided to be sold by him

22.explanation: “He decided to sell the house” preserves the original decision and its subject.

23.q: I remember them taking me to the zoo.

opts.a: I remember I am being taken to the zoo
opts.b: They are taking me to the zoo
opts.c: I remember being taken to the zoo
opts.d: I remember that I was taken to the zoo by them

23.explanation: The final key marks B, but B removes “I remember” and changes the statement into a present action. C is the passive equivalent. Because the printed key conflicts with meaning-preserving grammar, this question is held out from scoring pending clarification.

24.q: Byron is said to have lived on vinegar and potatoes.

opts.a: They say that Byron lived on vinegar and potatoes
opts.b: Byron lived on vinegar and potatoes is said by them
opts.c: Vinegar and potatoes are lived on by Byron
opts.d: People said that Byron was living on vinegar and potatoes

24.explanation: The passive report “is said to have lived” changes to the impersonal active report “They say that Byron lived…”

25.q: He expected us to offer him the job.

opts.a: To offer him the job by us was expected by him
opts.b: The job was expected to be offered by us
opts.c: He expects the job to offer by us
opts.d: He expected to be offered the job

25.explanation: The passive infinitive “to be offered” keeps the job as the thing he expected to receive.

26.q: Rajendra Prasad was one of the greatest Indian leaders. (Comparative)

opts.a: Rajendra Prasad was as great as other Indian leaders.
opts.b: Rajendra Prasad was not the weakest of Indian leaders.
opts.c: Rajendra Prasad was greater than most other Indian leaders.
opts.d: Rajendra Prasad was also as great as other Indian leaders.

26.explanation: “One of the greatest” becomes “greater than most” in the comparative degree.

opts.b: Who does not like to be praised?
opts.c: Do everyone like to be praised?
opts.d: Doesn’t everybody likes to be praised?

27.explanation: The rhetorical question “Who does not like to be praised?” preserves the general assertion.

28.q: I wish I were a queen. (Exclamatory)

opts.a: Alas! if I were a queen!
opts.b: Oh! to have been a queen!
opts.d: Alas! I want to be queen!

28.explanation: “Oh, to be a queen!” expresses the same wish exclamatorily.

29.explanation: “It is not always easy” conveys that difficulty occurs often without changing the statement to an absolute.

30.q: What though the field be lost? (Assertive)

opts.a: The field will be lost eventually
opts.b: We are going to lose the field
opts.d: It does not matter even if the field is lost

30.explanation: The rhetorical question means that losing the field would not matter.

31.q: She was asked not to loiter in the gallery. (Affirmative)

opts.a: She was forbidden to loiter in the gallery
opts.b: She was told that she could not loiter in the gallery
opts.c: They asked her not to loiter in the gallery
opts.d: They forbade her to loiter in the gallery

31.explanation: “She was forbidden to loiter” states the same prohibition affirmatively.

32.q: It is better to lend than borrow. (Positive)

opts.a: To lend is better than to borrow
opts.b: Borrowing is not as good as lending
opts.c: To borrow is not better than lending

32.explanation: The positive-degree comparison uses “not as good as”: borrowing is not as good as lending.

33.q: His father is the most honest of all. (Comparative)

opts.a: No one else is so honest as his father
opts.b: None is more honest than his father
opts.c: His father is more honest than anybody else
opts.d: His father is as honest as anybody else

33.explanation: The final key marks C, but A, B and C all express the same comparison here. Multiple options are defensible, so the question is held out from scoring pending clarification.
33.reviewNote: The official key marks C, but A, B and C are grammatically valid comparative forms; held out from scoring pending clarification.

34.q: I wonder who is waiting __________ the table next to ours.
34.explanation: “Wait on a table” means to serve the people seated there; “on” is the required preposition.

35.q: Those are actions __________ which you should be ashamed.

36.explanation: “Lifted onto the table” describes movement to a position on top of it.

37.explanation: The standard idiom is “tenacious of life,” meaning persistent or difficult to kill. “With life” is not the accepted collocation here, so option B is the independently supported answer despite the final key.

38.q: The bee came in __________ the door.
38.explanation: “Through the door” describes entering via the doorway.

39.q: It is dangerous to enter __________ the enemy’s camp.
39.explanation: “Enter into” is the construction expected by the printed options for movement into a place.

40.q: Minority aspirations cannot forever be kept in check __________ the gun.
40.explanation: The phrase “with the gun” indicates the means used to keep aspirations in check.

41.q: A good judge never gropes __________ the conclusion.
41.explanation: “Grope for” means to search uncertainly for something, including a conclusion.

42.q: Under this heavy load the bridge will give __________.
42.explanation: “Give way” means to collapse or yield under pressure.

43.q: They quarrelled with me __________ the division of the booty.
43.explanation: “Quarrel about” introduces the subject of a disagreement.

44.q: It is more of self-interest than service. (Identify the part of speech of the underlined words “self-interest”.)
44.explanation: “Self-interest” names a motive or concern, so it is a noun.

45.q: All spoke in his favour. (Identify the part of speech of the underlined word “All”.)
45.explanation: “All” stands in for all the people who spoke, so it is a pronoun.

46.q: As he was poor, I helped him. (Identify the part of speech of the underlined word “As”.)
46.explanation: “As” joins the reason clause to the main clause, so it is a conjunction.

47.q: I’m just coming. (Identify the part of speech of the underlined word “just”.)
47.explanation: “Just” modifies “coming” by indicating that the action is happening now/very soon, so it functions as an adverb.

48.q: This is the road by which he came. (Identify the part of speech of the underlined word “which”.)
48.explanation: “Which” is a relative pronoun introducing the clause “by which he came.”

49.q: Every member is present. (Identify the part of speech of the underlined word “Every”.)
49.explanation: In traditional school grammar, “every” is a distributive adjective modifying “member.”

50.q: He showed much patience. (Identify the part of speech of the underlined word “much”.)
50.explanation: “Much” modifies the noun “patience,” so it is an adjective of quantity in traditional grammar.

51.q: He said to her, “What a cold day!”

opts.a: He told her that it was a cold day.
opts.b: He exclaimed that it was a cold day.
opts.c: He exclaimed sorrowfully that it was a cold day.
opts.d: He exclaimed that it was a very cold day.

51.explanation: An exclamation of “What a cold day!” is reported with “exclaimed” and the intensifier “very.”

52.q: The father warned his son that he should be aware of him.

opts.a: The father warned his son, “Be aware of him!”
opts.b: The father warned his son, “Be careful of him.”
opts.c: The father warns his son, “Beware of him.”
opts.d: The father warns, “Son, be aware of him.”

52.explanation: The reported warning “should be aware” returns to the direct imperative “Be aware.”

53.q: Harish said to me, “Why didn’t you come with us?”

opts.a: Harish asked me why I did not come with them.
opts.b: Harish asked me why didn’t I go with them.
opts.c: Harish asked me why I did not go with them.
opts.d: Harish asked whether I want to go with them.

53.explanation: In reported questions, use statement word order and backshift “you/us” to “I/them.”

54.q: She said, “When I was a child, I wasn’t afraid of ghosts.”

opts.a: She said when she was a child she wasn’t afraid of ghosts.
opts.b: She told me that when she was a child she never feared ghosts.
opts.c: She said that when she was a child she wasn’t afraid of ghosts.
opts.d: She said that when she had been a child she wasn’t afraid of ghosts.

54.explanation: Option C reports the statement with the correct subject changes and preserves the past-time clause.

55.q: “If you don’t keep quiet I shall shoot you,” he said to her in a calm voice.

opts.a: He warned her to shoot if she didn’t keep quiet calmly.
opts.b: He said calmly that he shall shoot her if she doesn’t keep quiet.
opts.c: He warned her calmly that he would shoot her if she didn’t keep quiet.
opts.d: He warned with a calm voice that he should shoot if she is not quiet.

55.explanation: The threat is reported with “warned,” backshifted “would,” and the original condition.

56.q: A political leader appealing to popular desires and prejudices.
56.explanation: A demagogue seeks support by appealing to popular prejudices and emotions.

57.q: Not allowing the passage of light.
57.explanation: “Opaque” describes something that does not let light pass through.

58.explanation: “Slush” is partly melted snow or ice mixed with water.

59.explanation: A “coffle” is a line or group of enslaved people being transported together.

60.q: A person of humble beginning who has gained wealth.
60.explanation: A “parvenu” is someone of humble origin who has recently risen to wealth or status.

61.q:
Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.
A. Therefore, I bought a good house in a respectable neighbourhood.
B. This made me eager to welcome the first guest at home and show my hospitality.
C. I intended to be a model citizen in the neighbourhood.
D. I decided it was time for me to settle down.
61.explanation: The sequence is D–A–C–B: deciding to settle down leads to buying a house, then the intention to be a model neighbour, which motivates welcoming a first guest.

62.q: Four sentences are given: A. I sow a seed. B. I saw the sapling. C. I saw the sprout. D. I saw the plant. Select the correct order.
62.explanation: The natural growth sequence is seed, sprout, sapling, then plant: A–C–B–D.

63.q: Four sentences are given: A. When it saw me, it moved quickly and hid itself in a coconut shell. B. I quietly went near and closed the mouth of the coconut shell with a stone. C. One day I saw a small snake in the compound. D. It was crawling along slowly. Select the correct order.
63.explanation: The event proceeds from seeing the snake (C), to its slow movement (D), its hiding (A), and closing the shell (B).

64.q: Four sentences describe buying a product online: A. Add the product to your shopping cart. B. Select the brand you like. C. Enter the card details and buy the product online. D. Look for the product you want to purchase. Select the correct order.
64.explanation: First find the product (D), select its brand (B), add it to the cart (A), then enter payment details (C).

65.q: Four sentences describe a traffic incident: A. A man on a bike had to ride on the pavement. B. When he tried to plunge onto the road, a car hit him. C. As the bus inched through the evening life, the traffic grew. D. There was no space on the road any more. Select the correct order.
65.explanation: Traffic increases (C), the road runs out of space (D), the man rides on the pavement (A), and a car hits him when he tries to re-enter the road (B).

66.explanation: “Insubordinant” is misspelled; the standard adjective is “insubordinate.”

67.explanation: “Prosecuet” is misspelled; the correct spelling is “prosecute.”

68.explanation: “Leviathane” is misspelled; the correct spelling is “Leviathan.”

69.explanation: “Erradicate” is misspelled; the correct spelling is “eradicate.”

70.explanation: “Cromatic” is missing the h; the correct spelling is “chromatic.”

71.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of “admonish”.
71.explanation: “Admonish” means to warn or reprimand; “flatter” has the opposite sense.

72.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of “judicious”.
72.explanation: “Judicious” means showing good judgment; “indiscreet” is an appropriate opposite.

73.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of “bashful”.

74.q: Select the most appropriate antonym of “waver”.
74.explanation: “Waver” means to fluctuate or be unsteady; “steady” is its opposite.

75.explanation: “Turbid” means cloudy or unclear; “clear” is the antonym.

76.explanation: “Integrate” means to combine parts into a whole.

77.explanation: “Come in the way of” means obstruct or hinder. “Hamper” (D) is the matching choice; “deprive” (C) means take something away and does not fit the phrase.

81.q: The doctor with his interns are due to arrive here by noon. Identify the segment containing the grammatical error.
81.explanation: The head subject is the singular “doctor”; the verb should be “is due,” so the error is in “interns are due.”

82.q: Are you having your own transport to go home from work? Identify the segment containing the grammatical error.
82.explanation: For possession, use “Do you have your own transport?” rather than “Are you having.”

83.q: Where have you been from such a long time? Identify the segment containing the grammatical error.
83.explanation: Use “for” with a duration: “Where have you been for such a long time?”

84.q: Do you earn so much to make both ends meet? Identify the segment containing the grammatical error.
84.explanation: The intended construction is “earn enough to make both ends meet,” so “so much to” is incorrect.

85.q: Aren’t you such young to travel by yourself? Identify the segment containing the grammatical error.
85.explanation: Use “so young” before an adjective; “such” modifies a noun phrase.

86.q: Lali __________ taken a lesson on driving.
86.explanation: “Lali” is singular, so the present-perfect auxiliary is “has.”

87.explanation: “Was mending” is the grammatical past-continuous form for the action described.

88.q: These fruits __________ not be eaten by the patient.
88.explanation: The modal “will” forms the future passive: “will not be eaten.”

89.q: Zira __________ his future wife at the park.
89.explanation: The simple past “met” is the grammatical form for the completed event described.

90.q: The ants __________ working hard all winter.
90.explanation: “Have been working” is the present perfect continuous with the plural subject “ants.”

91.q: The police __________ having convicted the man.
91.explanation: “Denied having convicted” is the correct verb plus perfect gerund construction.

92.q: The kind woman __________ the little infant as her own.
92.explanation: “Mothers” is a verb meaning to care for someone as a mother would.

93.q: The dampness began to __________ the old man’s health.
93.explanation: After “began to,” use the base verb “affect”; here it means to harm or influence.

94.q: Linda __________ a gift from her husband.
94.explanation: “Receives” agrees with the singular subject Linda and completes the sentence.

95.q: You must __________ to the instructions given by the teacher.
95.explanation: The verb “listen” takes “to”: “listen to the instructions.” “Obey” takes a direct object without “to.”

97.explanation: “Incident” is the closest option to an occurrence or event surrounding a situation.

99.explanation: “Scrutiny” means close examination or inspection; “survey” is the closest listed option.

100.explanation: “Latent” means present but inactive or hidden.

37.explanation: The standard idiom is “tenacious of life,” meaning persistent or difficult to kill. “With life” is not the accepted collocation here, so option B is the independently supported answer despite the final key.

77.explanation: “Come in the way of” means obstruct or hinder. “Hamper” (D) is the matching choice; “deprive” (C) means take something away and does not fit the phrase.

aao-2024-arithmetic.evidence: Questions 1–100 have been checked against the printed pages (pages 1–10) and the final answer key. Stems, four options and calculations were verified. Q75 is held out for a key/ratio conflict, Q70 for a missing assumption, Q30 is compensated, and Q37 is editorially completed. Q100’s printed “board” is corrected to “broad” for readability. The item Q75 was independently re-keyed after checking its printed wording; the final key’s answer conflicts with the standard collocation/phrase or worked calculation.

1.q: The value of √2 up to three places of decimal is—
1.explanation: √2 ≈ 1.414213…, which rounds to 1.414 to three decimal places.

2.q: The smallest perfect square number which is divisible by 15, 24 and 25 is—
2.explanation: The least common multiple is 600. Its prime factorization is 2³·3·5²; to make all exponents even, multiply by 2·3=6, giving 3600.

3.q: The number 675 is to be multiplied by which smallest number so that the resulting number will become a perfect cube?
3.explanation: 675 = 3³·5². Multiplying by 5 makes the exponents multiples of three: 675×5 = 3³·5³ = 15³.

4.q: The value of 0.5777…… is—

5.explanation: Rationalize the denominator: (√7+√5)²/(7−5) = (12+2√35)/2 = 6+√35.

6.q: The HCF of two numbers is 16 and their LCM is 160. If one number is 32, then the other number is—
6.explanation: For two integers, their product is HCF×LCM. The other number is (16×160)/32 = 80.

7.q: The number of terms in the sequence 4, 11, 18, …, 186 is—
7.explanation: This is an arithmetic progression with first term 4 and common difference 7. Solve 4+(n−1)7=186 to get n=27.

8.q: The 8th term of the arithmetic progression 9, 6, 3, 0, … is—
8.explanation: The first term is 9 and the common difference is −3. The eighth term is 9+7(−3)=−12.

9.q: Rama gets 49% marks in an examination, obtaining 294 marks. The percentage of marks obtained by his friend in the same examination, who scores 372 marks, is—
9.explanation: 294 is 49% of 600, so the maximum is 600. The friend’s percentage is 372/600×100 = 62%.

10.q: If the length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and the breadth is decreased by 20%, then the area decreases by—
10.explanation: The new area factor is 1.20×0.80=0.96, so the area decreases by 4%.

11.q: A shopkeeper sells two shirts at ₹1995 each. On one he gains 5% and on the other he loses 5%. His gain or loss in the whole transaction is—
11.explanation: When two items are sold at the same price with equal gain/loss rates, the net result is a loss of 5²/100 = 0.25%.

12.q: What rate percent is one minute 48 seconds to an hour?
12.explanation: One minute 48 seconds is 108 seconds. As a share of an hour: 108/3600×100 = 3%.

13.q: Three numbers are in the ratio 2:3:5. If the sum of their squares is 1862, then the first number is—
13.explanation: Let the numbers be 2k, 3k and 5k. Then 38k²=1862, so k=7 and the first number is 14.

14.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 2:3 and if 8 is added to each of them, they become in the ratio 3:4. The numbers are—
14.explanation: Let them be 2x and 3x. Solving (2x+8)/(3x+8)=3/4 gives x=8, so the numbers are 16 and 24.

15.q: The average height of 30 students out of a class of 40 is 160 cm and that of the remaining students is 156 cm. The average height of the whole class is—
15.explanation: The total height is 30×160 + 10×156 = 6360 cm. Divide by 40 to get 159 cm.

16.q: The mean of ten numbers is 40. If the mean of the first five is 42 and that of the last four is 35, the 6th number is—
16.explanation: The ten-number total is 400. The first five sum to 210 and the last four to 140; subtracting these nine numbers leaves the sixth as 50.

17.q: The mean weight of 5 men is increased by 1 kg when one of them, whose weight is 60 kg, is replaced by a new man. The weight of the new man is—
17.explanation: Increasing the mean by 1 kg raises the total by 5 kg. The replacement therefore weighs 60+5=65 kg.

18.q: Two pipes fill a tank in 10 hours and 12 hours respectively, while a third pipe empties the full tank in 20 hours. If all three pipes operate simultaneously, in how much time will the tank be filled?
18.explanation: The net rate is 1/10+1/12−1/20 = 2/15 tank per hour, so filling takes 15/2 = 7.5 hours.

19.q: If 8 men can reap 80 hectares in 24 days, how many hectares can 36 men reap in 30 days?
19.explanation: Output is proportional to workers and days: 80×(36×30)/(8×24)=450 hectares.

20.q: The speed of a moving car is 36 km/hr. This speed in m/sec is—
20.explanation: Convert km/h to m/s by multiplying by 5/18: 36×5/18=10 m/s.

21.q: Two persons start from the same place and walk in opposite directions at 5 km/hr and 4 km/hr respectively. At the end of 3 hours, the distance between them is—
21.explanation: Their separation speed is 5+4=9 km/hr. In 3 hours they are 9×3=27 km apart.

22.q: “A” and “B” are 30 km apart and walk towards each other. “A” is walking at the rate of 4 km/hr and “B” at 6 km/hr. They will meet after—
22.explanation: Their combined closing speed is 4+6=10 km/hr. The meeting time is 30/10=3 hours.

23.q: While walking at 3/5 of the usual speed, a man reaches his destination 10 minutes late. What is his usual time to reach his destination?
23.explanation: At 3/5 speed, travel time becomes 5/3 of normal. The extra 2/3 of the normal time is 10 minutes, so the usual time is 15 minutes.

24.q: Liana’s age is 16 years and his elder sister’s age is 21 years. After how many years will the sum of their ages be 51 years?
24.explanation: Their current ages sum to 37. The total increases by 2 each year, so (51−37)/2=7 years.

25.q: On a plane ground, a man walks 18 m due south, then he turns to his left and walks 6 m due east. He again turns to his left and walks 10 m due north. How far is he now from the starting point?
25.explanation: He is 8 m south and 6 m east of the start. His distance is √(8²+6²)=10 m.

26.q: A sum of money becomes ₹2420 in 2 years and ₹2662 in 3 years. If interest is compounded annually, the rate of interest is—
26.explanation: The ratio of year-3 to year-2 amounts is 2662/2420=1.10, so the annual compound rate is 10%.

27.q: If the perimeter of a circle is numerically equal to the perimeter of a square, then the areas are in the ratio (take π = 22/7)—
27.explanation: Equal perimeters give square side s=πr/2. Thus circle:square area = πr²:s² = 4:π = 14:11 when π=22/7.

28.q: The length of the longest pole that can be kept in a room of dimensions (12 m × 9 m × 8 m) is—
28.explanation: The longest pole is the room’s space diagonal: √(12²+9²+8²)=√289=17 m.

29.q: The volume of a cubical solid is 2744 cm³. Its surface area is—
29.explanation: The cube side is ∛2744=14 cm. Its surface area is 6×14²=1176 cm².

30.q: How many bricks, each measuring (25 cm × 11.25 cm × 6 cm), will be required to construct a wall of dimensions (8 cm × 6 cm × 22.5 cm) if 1/10 of the volume of the wall is occupied by cement mortar?
30.explanation: The official key compensates this item. As printed, the wall dimensions are smaller than a single brick, so none of the listed counts is physically consistent. If the first two wall dimensions were intended to be metres, the calculation would give 5760, but that correction is not supported by the scan; this item is left unscored.
30.reviewNote: The MPSC final key compensates this item; the wall dimensions are smaller than one brick as printed, so it is held out from scoring.

31.q: A kite is flying at a certain height from the horizontal ground. The thread, 100 m long, attached to the kite is tied to a point on the ground. The inclination of the thread with the ground is 30°. How high from the ground is the kite flying?
31.explanation: The thread is the hypotenuse of a right triangle. Height=100×sin(30°)=50 m.

32.q: In tossing two coins, the probability of getting two heads is—
32.explanation: The equally likely outcomes are HH, HT, TH and TT; only HH has two heads, so the probability is 1/4.

33.q: A bag contains 4 white and some red balls. If the probability of drawing a red ball at random is double that of drawing a white ball, the number of red balls in the bag is—
33.explanation: Let r be the number of red balls. r/(r+4)=2·4/(r+4), so r=8.

34.q: In a committee, 32 people speak Hindi, 14 speak English and 8 speak both Hindi and English. How many speak at least one of the two languages?
34.explanation: By inclusion–exclusion, 32+14−8=38 people speak at least one language.

35.q: In a survey of 200 students in a school, it was found that 125 like orange, 90 like apple and 60 like both orange and apple. How many like neither orange nor apple?
35.explanation: The number who like at least one is 125+90−60=155. Therefore 200−155=45 like neither.

36.q: The cost of a mobile handset is ₹20,000. A lady purchased it by paying ₹12,000 and the balance is to be cleared in two equal instalments of ₹4,500 each. What is the total interest charged under the instalment scheme?
36.explanation: The instalments total ₹9,000 against a financed balance of ₹8,000, so the interest is ₹1,000.

39.q: Metallic spheres of radii 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm respectively are melted to form a single solid sphere. The radius of the resulting sphere is—
39.explanation: Volume is conserved: R³=3³+4³+5³=216, so the new radius is 6 cm.

44.q: Find the smallest multiple of 2352 which is a perfect square.
44.explanation: 2352=2⁴×3×7². Multiply by 3 to make all prime exponents even: 2352×3=7056=84².

45.q: The list price of a shirt is ₹220. A discount of 20% is announced on festival sale. What is the selling price of the shirt?
45.explanation: A 20% discount is ₹44, so the selling price is ₹220−₹44=₹176.

54.q: If 45% of the students in a school are boys and the number of girls in the school is 605, how many boys are there in the school?
54.explanation: Girls are 55% of the total, so total students=605/0.55=1100. Boys=45%×1100=495.

55.q: A wire, when bent in the form of a square, encloses an area of 121 cm². The same wire is bent in the form of a circle. Find the radius of the circle.

63.explanation: Let g be the green balls. Since both probabilities have the same total denominator, 12/(12+g)=3g/(12+g), so g=4.

64.q: A card is drawn from a well-shuffled deck of 52 cards. Find the probability that the card drawn is neither a King nor a Queen.
64.explanation: There are 4 Kings and 4 Queens, leaving 44 acceptable cards. The probability is 44/52=11/13.

68.q: How many two-digit numbers are divisible by 3?
68.explanation: The two-digit multiples of 3 run from 12 to 99. Their count is (99−12)/3+1=30.

69.q: If p−2, p+1 and 2p−1 are in A.P., the value of p is—
69.explanation: In an arithmetic progression, consecutive differences are equal: (p+1)−(p−2)=3 and (2p−1)−(p+1)=p−2. Thus p=5.

93.explanation: Let B’s rate be r and A’s 2r. Then 3r=1/12, so r=1/36; B alone takes 36 days.

94.q: A can do a work in 36 days while B can do the same in 48 days. If A works for x days while B works for x+2 days, then one-third of the work is complete. Find x.
94.explanation: A’s rate is 1/36 and B’s is 1/48. Thus x/36+(x+2)/48=1/3. Multiplying by 144 gives 4x+3x+6=48, so x=6.

1.direction:
Directions (Question Nos. 1–7): Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. Your answers must be based on the passage only.

Climate change is an unprecedented challenge that threatens ecosystems, economies, and societies worldwide. The persistent rise in global temperatures, largely due to anthropogenic activities, has led to calamitous consequences such as extreme weather events, rising sea levels, and biodiversity loss. Scientists have attributed this phenomenon to the excessive emission of greenhouse gases, particularly carbon dioxide and methane, which trap heat within the earth’s atmosphere, exacerbating the warming effect.

One of the most ominous repercussions of climate change is the accelerated melting of polar ice caps, which contributes to rising sea levels and threatens coastal communities. This detrimental shift has led to the displacement of populations, loss of arable land, and an increase in natural disasters. Furthermore, fluctuating weather patterns have disrupted agricultural productivity, leading to food shortages and economic instability.

Governments and environmental organizations have initiated concerted efforts to mitigate climate change through renewable energy adoption, reforestation projects, and carbon reduction policies. However, despite these interventions, the planet continues to experience incessant climatic changes that necessitate immediate global cooperation. The pivotal role of individuals in reducing their carbon footprint, advocating for policy changes, and embracing sustainable lifestyles cannot be overstated.

Climate change is an unprecedented challenge that threatens ecosystems, economies, and societies worldwide. The persistent rise in global temperatures, largely due to anthropogenic activities, has led to calamitous consequences such as extreme weather events, rising sea levels, and biodiversity loss. Scientists have attributed this phenomenon to the excessive emission of greenhouse gases, particularly carbon dioxide and methane, which trap heat within the earth’s atmosphere, exacerbating the warming effect.

One of the most ominous repercussions of climate change is the accelerated melting of polar ice caps, which contributes to rising sea levels and threatens coastal communities. This detrimental shift has led to the displacement of populations, loss of arable land, and an increase in natural disasters. Furthermore, fluctuating weather patterns have disrupted agricultural productivity, leading to food shortages and economic instability.

Governments and environmental organizations have initiated concerted efforts to mitigate climate change through renewable energy adoption, reforestation projects, and carbon reduction policies. However, despite these interventions, the planet continues to experience incessant climatic changes that necessitate immediate global cooperation. The pivotal role of individuals in reducing their carbon footprint, advocating for policy changes, and embracing sustainable lifestyles cannot be overstated.

8.direction:
Directions (Question Nos. 8–15): Read the given passage carefully and answer the questions that follow. Your answers must be based on the passage only.

Reading good books is an indispensable habit that enriches the mind, fosters intellectual growth, and broadens one’s perspective. A well-written book serves as an illustrious guide, offering wisdom that transcends time and geography. Books expose readers to profound ideas, stimulate critical thinking, and cultivate a sense of curiosity. Those who engage in thoughtful reading develop a more astute understanding of the world and a refined ability to articulate their thoughts.

The habit of reading not only enhances knowledge but also refines linguistic skills. A lucid and well-structured book improves vocabulary, comprehension, and analytical abilities. Additionally, reading provides an escape from mundane realities, allowing individuals to immerse themselves in the captivating narratives of fiction or the erudite insights of non-fiction. Such engagement strengthens cognitive faculties, improves concentration, and fortifies memory.

Beyond intellectual benefits, books offer solace during turbulent times. The written word has the power to ameliorate stress, evoke empathy, and foster emotional resilience. Readers often find comfort in literature that resonates with their own experiences, helping them navigate personal dilemmas with newfound clarity. In an era dominated by digital distractions, cultivating a deep engagement with books can be a formidable antidote to fragmented attention and superficial content consumption.

Ultimately, reading good books is not merely a pastime but a quintessential practice for personal and intellectual growth. It nurtures creativity, instils wisdom, and enriches the human experience in ways that few other activities can. Developing the discipline to read regularly is a laudable endeavour—one that rewards the mind and spirit in immeasurable ways.

1.q:
Write a précis of the following passage (10 marks):

Drug abuse is a growing concern for law enforcement worldwide. It not only harms individuals but also fuels crime and destabilizes societies. Despite strict regulations, drug traffickers continue to evolve, using advanced technologies and underground networks to evade authorities. The illegal drug trade remains a major challenge, requiring strong enforcement, intelligence operations, and international cooperation.

Public awareness campaigns and rehabilitation programs play a crucial role in preventing substance abuse and supporting recovery. Community involvement is equally important in protecting vulnerable individuals, especially the youth. While law enforcement agencies lead the fight, every responsible citizen must support anti-drug initiatives to create a safer, drug-free society.
1.explanation: A précis should retain the passage’s main idea in concise language: drug abuse harms people and society, so effective prevention requires law enforcement, international cooperation, rehabilitation, public awareness and community support. Use your own words and give the précis an appropriate title.

2.q: As a concerned citizen of your city, write a formal letter to the Secretary, Excise & Narcotics Department requesting strict action against illegal drug activities in your locality. Highlight the increasing drug abuse problems, its impact on youth, and suggest measures for stricter enforcement and public awareness. (15 marks)
2.explanation: A strong response should use formal letter format, identify the local concern, explain the risks of drug abuse to young people, and propose practical enforcement and awareness measures. Award marks for clarity, organization, relevant details, and correct formal English.

3.q:
Read the passage and answer the questions below.

The ‘Little Tramp’, the unforgettable character Charlie Chaplin invented, was born purely by accident in 1915. While rushing to a film shoot in California, he grabbed clothes other people had left behind in the changing room and, when he emerged, he found he had created a personality everybody loved: a little guy in a bowler hat, a close-fitting jacket, a cane, out-sized shoes and a brush-like moustache.

Before long, Chaplin found himself a star. That puzzled him, for he saw himself essentially as a shy British Music Hall comedian. The U.S. acknowledged him as its king of silent film comedy. Soon, so did crowds all over the world. But life wasn’t always a laugh for Charles Spencer Chaplin. Both his parents were Music Hall artists, who separated when Charlie was very young. His childhood was very sad, for his mother never earned enough to look after Charlie and his older brother, Sydney. Sometimes, Chaplin had to sleep on the streets and forage for food in the garbage.

Charlie took his first bow on stage when his mother made her last appearance. It happened when her voice broke during a song. Her son stepped on stage and sang a popular song. That’s when a star was born. Through all these years of success, Charlie never forgot his troubled childhood. It made him recall a Christmas when he was denied two oranges and his bag of sweets for breaking a rule at the orphanage he went to after his mother’s death. It would have broken his heart if the other children had not offered him a share of theirs. Spontaneously, the adult Chaplin gifted the orphanage with a motion picture machine and insisted that each child should have as many oranges and sweets as they pleased.

(a) Which unforgettable character did Charlie Chaplin invent? (2)
(b) Describe the personality created by Charlie, whom everybody loved. (2)
(c) What did Charlie see himself as? (2)
(d) Give two reasons to show that Charlie Chaplin’s early life was very sad. (2)
(e) When did Charlie Chaplin start his career? (2)
(f) Choose the word in the passage that means ‘to search for food’: (i) stepped (ii) forage (iii) emerged (iv) orphanage. (1)
(g) Choose the meaning of ‘invented’: (i) created (ii) wrote (iii) struggled (iv) laughed. (1)
(h) Find the word in the passage opposite in meaning to ‘bold’: (i) found (ii) shy (iii) silent (iv) puzzled. (1)
(i) Find the word in the passage opposite in meaning to ‘failure’: (i) troubled (ii) share (iii) motion (iv) success. (1)
(j) Find the word in the passage similar in meaning to ‘appeared’: (i) insisted (ii) offered (iii) emerged (iv) broken. (1)
3.explanation: Answer guide: (a) the Little Tramp; (b) a little man wearing a bowler hat, close-fitting jacket, carrying a cane, with oversized shoes and a brush-like moustache; (c) a shy British Music Hall comedian; (d) his parents separated, the family was poor, and he sometimes slept on the streets and searched rubbish for food; (e) when his mother’s voice broke during a song and he stepped on stage to sing. Objective choices: (f) forage (ii), (g) created (i), (h) shy (ii), (i) success (iv), (j) emerged (iii). The source prints two marks for (a)–(e) and one for (f)–(j).

2.q:
Write a précis of the following passage by reducing it to one third of its length (10 marks):

Reading is one of the most valuable habits a person can develop. It opens up new worlds, ideas, and perspectives, enriching the mind and imagination. Through books, articles, and other written materials, people gain knowledge about history, science, culture, and human behaviour. Reading also improves language skills, vocabulary, and critical thinking. It encourages curiosity and creativity, allowing individuals to explore concepts beyond their immediate experiences. Furthermore, reading can be a source of relaxation and stress relief, offering an escape from the pressures of daily life. In a world full of distractions, dedicating time to reading helps cultivate discipline and focus. Societies that encourage reading tend to be more informed, empathetic, and innovative. Thus, reading is not merely a pastime but a lifelong tool for personal growth and societal advancement.
2.explanation: Write a concise précis of about one third the passage’s length in your own words. Preserve its central ideas: reading builds knowledge, language and critical thinking; supports curiosity, focus and relaxation; and contributes to personal and social growth. Give it a suitable title and avoid adding opinions.

4.q:
Read the following passage and answer the questions based on it:

Studies serve for delight, for ornament, and for ability. Their chief use for delight is in privateness and retiring; for ornament is in this course; and for ability is in the judgment and disposition of business. For expert men can execute, and perhaps judge of particulars, one by one; but the general counsels, and the plots and marshalling of affairs, come best, from those that are learned. To spend too much time in studies is sloth; to use them too much for ornaments is affectation; to make judgement wholly by their rules, is the humour of a scholar. They perfect nature, and are perfected by experience: for natural abilities are like natural plants that need pruning, by study; and studies themselves do give forth directions too much at large, except they be bounded in by experience. Crafty men condemn studies, simple men admire them, and wise men use them; for they teach not their own use; but that is a wisdom without them, and above them, won by observation. Read not to contradict and confute; nor to believe and take for granted; nor to find talk and discourse but to weigh and consider.

(a) According to the author, why should one study? (2 marks)
(b) Why does the author not recommend too much of studies? (2 marks)
(c) According to the author, how can studies be perfected? (2 marks)
(d) Which kind of human beings denounce studies? (2 marks)
(e) According to the author, why should one read? (2 marks)
4.explanation: Suggested answers: (a) Studies serve for delight, ornament and ability. (b) Too much time in study is sloth; using studies chiefly for ornament is affectation; judging only by study rules is the humour of a scholar. (c) Experience perfects studies. (d) Crafty men condemn studies. (e) Read to weigh and consider, not merely to contradict, accept without question, or make conversation.

2.q:
Write a précis of the following passage (10 marks):
Self-reliance is the pilgrim’s best staff, the worker’s best tool. It is the master key that unlocks all the difficulties of life. “Help yourself and Heaven will help you” is a maxim that receives daily confirmation. He who begins with crutches will generally end with crutches. Help from within always strengthens, but help from without invariably weakens the recipients. The habit of depending upon others should be vigorously resisted, since it tends to weaken the intellectual faculties and paralyse the judgement. The struggle against adverse circumstances has, on the contrary, a strengthening effect, like that of the pure mountain air on an enfeebled frame.

This is a lesson which is not taught in academic institutions nowadays. The vice of the modern system of education is that it lays down too many royal roads to knowledge. The difficulties, which formerly compelled the student to think and labour for himself are now removed. The race of thorough and complete scholars is dying out. Our young men are equipped to such an extent with manuals that explain everything and guides that go everywhere, that they find no occasion for thought. Why take any trouble at all when so many are willing to relieve you of it?
2.explanation: Sample précis (title: “The Value of Self-Reliance”): Self-reliance strengthens judgement and character. Depending constantly on others weakens independent thought, while facing difficulties develops intellectual ability. Education should therefore encourage students to think and work for themselves instead of relying entirely on ready-made guides. A good précis should be concise, use the writer’s main ideas and be expressed in the student’s own words.

17.q: Make sentences with any five idioms/phrases to show their meaning: (a) Hold water; (b) Bird’s-eye view; (c) Apple-pie order; (d) To miss the bus; (e) A small fry; (f) Gordian knot; (g) Damp squib. (5×2=10 marks)
17.explanation: Sample uses: Her explanation does not hold water. From the hill we had a bird’s-eye view of the town. The files were arranged in apple-pie order. He missed the bus by arriving late. The manager treated no employee as a small fry. The mediator cut through the Gordian knot. The much-advertised event was a damp squib.

18.q: Change the voice: (a) The chef is cooking a special dish. (b) How did you open the door? (c) Tea shall not be taken by me today. (d) By whom were you insulted? (e) Mistakes were made. (5×2=10 marks)
18.explanation: Possible answers: (a) A special dish is being cooked by the chef. (b) How was the door opened? (c) I shall not take tea today. (d) Who insulted you? (e) Someone made mistakes. Passive sentences without an expressed agent may allow more than one natural active subject.

19.q: Complete the question tags: (a) Let us go, ___? (b) He isn’t very happy with it, ___? (c) Mind your business, ___? (d) Keep your mouth shut, ___? (e) Don’t break the glass, ___? (5×2=10 marks)
19.explanation: Suggested tags: (a) shall we? (b) is he? (c) will you? (d) will you? (e) will you? Commands commonly take “will you?” as the tag.

20.q: Rewrite as directed: (a) How long have you ___ him? (use “know”); (b) The sun was shining. We went for a walk. (make compound); (c) Having finished his work, he went home. (make complex); (d) You have to pay or you cannot leave this place. (make simple); (e) She said, “You see, you cannot meet the principal.” (indirect speech); (f) Portia exclaimed with sorrow that she was ruined. (direct speech); (g) Waste not, want not. (begin with “if”); (h) I do not know her nature any better than you. (use positive degree); (i) His prompt reply will able us to take timely action. (correct/improve); (j) Shall we ever forget these happy days? (rewrite using “never”). (10×2=20 marks)
20.explanation: Possible answers: (a) How long have you known him? (b) The sun was shining, so we went for a walk. (c) After he had finished his work, he went home. (d) You cannot leave this place without paying. (e) She said that I could not meet the principal. (f) Portia exclaimed, “Alas! I am ruined!” (g) If you do not waste, you will not want. (h) I know her nature no better than you do. (i) His prompt reply will enable us to take timely action. (j) We shall never forget these happy days.

5.explanation: “Sang-froid” means calmness and composure, especially under pressure (C).

8.explanation: “Loaves and fishes” refers to material or worldly benefits (D).

10.q: Which statement is false according to the passage?

11.q: What crisis are cement-tile manufacturers facing, according to the passage?

12.q: Which word has the same meaning as “idle” as used in the passage?
12.explanation: In this passage, “idle capacity” means capacity that is unused. None of the options gives that contextual meaning; “lazy” describes a person, so the item is held out.

13.q: Which statement is correct according to the passage?

opts.a: White cement is not used to manufacture paint
opts.b: White cement is a minor part of tile manufacturing
opts.c: White cement is very important for tile manufacturing
opts.d: White cement is used only to make paint

13.explanation: The passage identifies white cement as a basic raw material used extensively to produce cement tiles and cement paint; C is the only statement consistent with it.

14.q: What does the author suggest to bring down prices?

opts.a: The Government should control the white-cement market
opts.c: Use of white cement in other areas should be reduced

16.explanation: “Chances” is a countable plural noun, so the comparative “fewer” is the standard choice (D).

17.q: A horse is ____ like an elephant.
17.explanation: “A horse is not like an elephant” is the grammatical sentence (A).

18.q: I injured my knee four years ago, but I have been feeling pain in it ____.
18.explanation: “Ever since” refers back to the injury four years ago and describes pain continuing from then to the present (D).

19.q: Have you received any letter from your son ____?
19.explanation: Both “lately” and “of late” are grammatical adverbs meaning “recently” in this question. The item has two defensible options and is held out.

20.explanation: The standard phrase is “comes from a good family” (D).

27.explanation: The speaker recommends what the listener should do, so the sentence expresses advice (C).

28.explanation: “May you live long!” is an optative expression of a wish (D).

29.q: The manager said to his assistant, “Let the customers in.” This is an expression of:

30.explanation: “Will be waiting” is the future progressive construction (B).

31.q: The verdict of the Judges that he is guilty has been challenged. Identify the sentence type.
31.explanation: “That he is guilty” is a subordinate noun clause in apposition to “verdict”; the sentence has a main clause and a subordinate clause, so it is complex (C).

32.q: He denied to have sold spurious drugs to the customers. Identify the sentence type.
32.explanation: The sentence contains one independent clause; “to have sold spurious drugs” is an infinitive phrase, not a finite subordinate clause. It is simple (B).

33.q: Morning walk is a good exercise, therefore everybody should walk. Identify the sentence type.
33.explanation: The sentence joins two independent clauses: “Morning walk is a good exercise” and “everybody should walk.” It is compound (A).

34.q: Everyone wonders how she completed this work. Identify the sentence type.
34.explanation: “How she completed this work” is a subordinate noun clause completing “wonders”; the sentence is complex (C).

35.q: Although they were tired, they worked late into the night. Identify the sentence type.
35.explanation: “Although they were tired” is a dependent adverb clause, so the sentence is complex (C).

36.q: You permit me and I shall leave the room. Identify the sentence type.
36.explanation: The sentence has two independent clauses joined by “and,” so it is compound (A).

37.q: **Rich as he is**, he is not happy. Identify the clause type of the underlined words.
37.explanation: “Rich as he is” is a concessive subordinate adverb clause (C).

38.q: I do not know **whom she is teaching**. Identify the clause type of the underlined words.
38.explanation: “Whom she is teaching” is the object of “know,” so it is a noun clause (A).

39.q: He told me **what his father told him**. Identify the clause type of the underlined words.
39.explanation: “What his father told him” is the content of what he told me and functions as a noun clause (B).

40.q: I shall go to the place **where my friend lives**. Identify the clause type of the underlined words.
40.explanation: “Where my friend lives” modifies “place” and is a relative/adjective clause. The scan offers both “relative clause” (A) and “adjective clause” (B), so there is no unique answer.
40.reviewNote: “Where my friend lives” modifies “place” and is a relative/adjective clause. The scan offers both “relative clause” (A) and “adjective clause” (B), so there is no unique answer.

41.q: **He could not utter a single word to his son** who, when he arrived, was in a dejected mood. Identify the clause type of the underlined words.
41.explanation: The underlined words form the main independent clause; they are the principal clause (C).

42.q: **Since my brother came**, he has been teaching. Identify the clause type of the underlined words.
42.explanation: “Since my brother came” gives the time of the teaching and is a subordinate adverb clause (B).

43.q: The prisoner was released on ____ for good behaviour.
43.explanation: Parole is conditional release from prison, commonly granted for good behaviour (C).

44.q: The brilliant students will be ____ scholarships.

45.q: The salt spray has gradually ____ the bridge.
45.explanation: Salt spray gradually wears away a structure, so “eroded” is the best fit (A).

46.q: On seeing the police approach, the miscreants ____.
46.explanation: “Took to their heels” means ran away, which fits the context (C).

47.q: If a speech is full of pompous words, it is ____.
47.explanation: “Bombastic” and “grandiloquent” both describe pompous, inflated language; the options do not support a unique answer.
47.reviewNote: “Bombastic” and “grandiloquent” both describe pompous, inflated language; the options do not support a unique answer.

1.explanation: Choose one topic and stay within 300 words. 1.explanation: Mizoram was officially declared India’s first fully literate state on 20 May 2025. “Fully literate” is the government programme designation based on the state’s literacy threshold, rather than a claim that every resident can read.

2.explanation: On 5 August 2025, a cloudburst in the Dharali area of Uttarkashi triggered a destructive flash flood; contemporaneous reports recorded at least four deaths and many people missing.

12.explanation: The Bairabi–Sairang railway line is 51.38 km long, according to the Ministry of Railways/PIB project and inauguration information.

13.explanation: The Noble Eightfold Path is a core teaching of Buddhism and the path leading toward the cessation of suffering.

Q1–20 were checked against the printed cover and pages 1–2; all numbered stems, option wording and four-option sets were compared with the scan. The cover specifies 100 one-mark questions and two hours, with no negative-marking instruction. Nineteen answers have independently derived explanations. Q14 is held because “within India’s boundary” can refer to India’s claimed boundary (K2) or territory under Indian administration (Kangchenjunga), and the stem does not specify which. Questions 21–40 were checked against printed pages 2–4; stems, numbering and all options were verified. All twenty have independently derived explanations. Q24 is clarified to distinguish Presidential assent (15 June) from the Act coming into force (12 October). Questions 41–60 were checked against printed pages 4–6; all stems and option sets were checked for completeness and legibility. All twenty have independently derived explanations. Q44’s expected season was checked against the Lai District Government’s festival description; Q52’s award was checked against the Urban Mobility India award record. Questions 61–80 were checked against printed pages 6–7; all stems, numbering and options were checked. All twenty have independently derived explanations. Q64 spelling and Q68 longitude typography/options were corrected for readability; Q75 was clarified because the phrase “first defined” was historically imprecise, while the Brundtland Report contains the widely used definition. Questions 81–100 were checked against printed pages 7–8; all stems, numbering and four-option sets were verified against the scan. Twenty answers have independently derived explanations. Q95 is keyed to the mismatched Duhmanga–Thanghniangi pair after checking Mizo Studies (Mizoram University) and the Tribal Research Institute folklore catalogue; Q90 uses “genotype” as the closest available choice, though “genome” is technically more exact for a complete genetic complement. Q81 was verified against the Ramsar site record and Q86 against the Tamil Nadu State Wetlands Authority.
